Hindu tradition traces the Kumbh to the Samudra Manthan, the churning of the ocean by the devas and asuras in search of amrit. When the kalash of amrit emerged, four places became joined to its story: Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nashik and Ujjain. The timing of each Kumbh follows the Sun, the Moon and Jupiter; at Haridwar it is held when Jupiter is in Aquarius (Kumbha) and the Sun in Aries. Haridwar is where the Ganga leaves the Himalaya and enters the plains. Its previous Kumbh was held in 2021. The official website names this gathering Haridwar Kumbh 2027; the Maharashtra Kumbh authority lists Haridwar's mela as a Kumbh or Ardh Kumbh.

en: Har Ki Pauri, Haridwar, on the Ganga: the official schedule lists every bathing day here.

On the Amrit Snan days the thirteen akharas go to the ghats in procession, with saints, Naga sadhus and Mahamandaleshwars, for the ceremonial bath. The official website describes it as the holiest bathing ritual of the Mela.
On every day of the Mela, pilgrims bathe at the ghats, offer prayers, perform rituals and seek the blessings of the Ganga.
A Kumbh bath is traditionally taken with a sankalp: saying who you are, where and when you are bathing, and with what intention.
After the bath, the usual sequence is daan (charity), japa, meditation and darshan of sadhus and saints.
Through the Mela there are satsangs and discourses, processions, and aarti and prayers by the Ganga.

value.en: Kumbh means a pitcher or kalash, and the mela recalls the kalash of amrit from the churning of the ocean. The Kumbh comes to each of its four places, Haridwar, Prayagraj, Ujjain and Nashik–Trimbakeshwar, roughly once every twelve years, close to the time Jupiter takes to pass through all twelve signs. At Nashik and Trimbakeshwar it is held when Jupiter and the Sun are in Leo (Simha), which is why it is called the Simhastha. It falls in the monsoon months of Shravan and Bhadrapad, on the Godavari, which rises on Brahmagiri above Trimbakeshwar. In 2017 UNESCO inscribed the Kumbh Mela on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

en: Ramtirth, in the Panchavati area of Nashik: by tradition Shri Ram, Sita and Lakshman stayed at Panchavati on the Godavari during the forest exile. Vaishnava sadhus bathe here.
Kushavarta Tirth, Trimbakeshwar, about 30 km away: Trimbakeshwar is one of the twelve jyotirlingas, near the source of the Godavari on Brahmagiri. Shaiva sadhus bathe here.

sourceRefs.publisher: Nashik Trimbakeshwar Kumbh Mela Authority, Government of Maharashtra

en: Dhwajarohan, the hoisting of the flag on 31 October 2026, opens the Simhastha; Dhwajavatarana, the lowering of the flag on 24 July 2028, closes it.
Nagar Pradakshina, the traditional procession around Nashik, is held before the Amrit Snans.
On the third Amrit Snan the akharas bathe by tradition: Vaishnava sadhus at Ramtirth on 11 September, Shaiva sadhus at Kushavarta on 12 September.
A Kumbh bath is traditionally taken with a sankalp: saying who you are, where and when you are bathing, and with what intention.
After the bath, the usual sequence is daan (charity), japa, meditation and darshan of sadhus and saints.
Beyond the Amrit Snan days, the authority lists many other auspicious bathing days at Ramtirth and Kushavarta through the Simhastha.
